$comment: The first verification board. Every panel and touch value here is measured and recorded in docs/hardware.md with its provenance. The bundle partition is a decision, not a measurement: 1 MB to start, bounded by this board's 16 MB flash, revised only by the measurement of T7.2. The asset partition is a decision too, taken by the owner on 2026-09-27 (spec 006, RF-145): 1 MB directly after the bundle, bounded by the same flash.
name: sunton-8048s050c

capabilities.$comment: What this board carries beyond the panel (spec 009, RF-255). Storage is the platform's own non-volatile storage, whose partition the pipeline generates for every profile, so the entry names the capability and the hardware it needs is nothing.

card.$comment: The TF socket in SPI mode. The pins are declared by the owner reference project, Sunton5_IDF, components/Sunton5_IDF/include/sunton5_board.h, whose SD section records that the native four-bit interface is not routed on this board; spec 012 T012.13 confirms them here and moves the row in docs/hardware.md from declared to measured.

link.$comment: The board's own radio interface: the platform's WiFi driver, no module and no pin of its own. Spec 013 T013.14 joins the desk's network with it.

fetch.$comment: HTTP over the link. It carries no hardware of its own: the requests go over the link this board already declares, and the certificate store is the build's own bundle (spec 014).

bundlePartition.$comment: The factory app partition takes everything between 0x10000 and this offset, so the offset is what sizes the application. It moved from 0x210000 to 0x410000 on 2026-10-01: the HTTP client and the certificate bundle spec 014 adds took the image to 2033248 B, which left three per cent of a two megabyte partition and no room for the pool. Four megabytes is the same lever the derivation already gives, and this board's flash has eleven megabytes unclaimed below it.
bundlePartition.name: bundle
